title: Easy weeknight dinners for the first real weeks of fall
dek: As evenings get darker, a few simple, warm dinners make Tuesday nights feel a lot less rushed.
body: It is six o'clock, and the light outside is already starting to fade earlier than it did a month ago. Somewhere in my house, someone is asking what is for dinner.

This is the time of year when I lean on a short list of easy, warm meals. A pot of soup with whatever vegetables are in the fridge. A sheet pan of chicken and potatoes that roasts while I change out of work clothes. Pasta with a jar of sauce and something green on the side.

None of these are fancy, and that is the point. On a Tuesday, I want a dinner that gets everyone fed without a lot of dishes or decisions. The warmth of the oven and the smell of something cooking does a lot to make a house feel settled.
I also try to make a little extra, so tomorrow's lunch is already taken care of. That one habit saves me time and money through the whole week.
Tonight, pick one meal you can make without a recipe, and double it so tomorrow is a little easier.
